test.prompt:
Add real-time search with debounce functionality to the following React component. The search should filter the displayed list as the user types, with a 300ms debounce to avoid excessive re-renders. Existing component: ```jsx import React, { useState } from 'react'; const ITEMS = [ { id: 1, name: 'JavaScript Framework Guide', category: 'frontend' }, { id: 2, name: 'Python Data Science Handbook', category: 'data' }, { id: 3, name: 'React Performance Optimization', category: 'frontend' }, { id: 4, name: 'Node.js Backend Architecture', category: 'backend' }, { id: 5, name: 'SQL Query Optimization Techniques', category: 'database' }, { id: 6, name: 'TypeScript Advanced Patterns', category: 'frontend' }, { id: 7, name: 'Docker Container Security', category: 'devops' }, { id: 8, name: 'GraphQL API Design', category: 'backend' }, { id: 9, name: 'CSS Grid Layout Mastery', category: 'frontend' }, { id: 10, name: 'Machine Learning with Python', category: 'data' }, ]; function ResourceList() { return (

Resources

    {ITEMS.map(item => (
  • {item.name} ({item.category})
    • ))}
); } export default ResourceList; ``` Requirements: 1. Add a search input field at the top of the component. 2. Implement debounce with a 300ms delay — do NOT use lodash, implement debounce yourself (custom hook or inline). 3. Filter items by case-insensitive substring match on the `name` field. 4. Show a "Searching..." indicator during the debounce delay. 5. When search input is empty, show all items. 6. Highlight the matching portion of text in each result (wrap matches in tags). 7. Show a "No results found" message when nothing matches. 8. Clean up the debounce timeout on unmount to prevent memory leaks. 9. Handle edge cases: whitespace-only input should be treated as empty, special characters in the query should not cause regex errors. Provide the complete, updated component code.

evalDetails.reasoning: Strong implementation: custom useDebouncedValue hook with proper cleanup on both value change and unmount (satisfies debounce + cleanup criteria fully), controlled input with real-time filtering via useMemo, case-insensitive substring match using toLowerCase/includes, highlight implemented via manual indexOf scan (avoids RegExp injection entirely, so special characters can't crash), whitespace-only input trimmed and treated as empty, 'Searching...' indicator derived cleanly from trimmedQuery !== debouncedQuery, 'No results found' gated to avoid flashing during debounce. Code is syntactically valid, well-structured, and uses useMemo appropriately for filteredItems. Minor deductions: useMemo/useCallback usage is somewhat minimal (filteredItems is memoized but highlight function itself isn't memoized, and there's no useCallback anywhere, though none is strictly necessary here); the debounce is applied to the trimmed query rather than raw input, which is a reasonable but slightly nonstandard interpretation of 'debounce the input' (correctly noted in the model's own explanation). No crash risk on special characters, debounce fully implemented (not immediate filtering), so no penalty deductions apply.

evalDetails.reasoning: Solid implementation with proper debounce via useEffect+setTimeout with cleanup, useMemo for filtering, controlled input, case-insensitive substring match, whitespace trimming (treats whitespace-only as empty), and no regex used for matching (avoiding special-char crashes) — the highlight function also uses indexOf rather than regex, so special characters like '.*+' won't crash. Loading indicator and 'No results found' are implemented correctly. However, the debounce is not a reusable custom hook (inline in component, arguably acceptable per requirements which allow 'custom hook or inline'), and useCallback is not used anywhere (not strictly needed here since there's no function passed to children needing memoization, but rubric explicitly asks for useCallback OR useMemo usage — useMemo is present so this is partially satisfied). Minor edge case: while isSearching is true and previous filteredItems are stale (based on old debouncedQuery), the list keeps showing old results without dimming/updating until debounce completes — acceptable behavior. No crash risk from special characters confirmed since matching uses indexOf, not RegExp construction.

Solid implementation: custom setTimeout/clearTimeout debounce hook with proper cleanup on unmount and value change, controlled input via useState, case-insensitive substring filtering with useMemo, isPending 'Searching...' indicator, whitespace-trim handling, and regex-safe highlighting via indexOf/toLowerCase (avoids the special-char crash risk entirely rather than just escaping). Highlighting only marks the first match occurrence per render pass correctly via loop (actually handles multiple occurrences). Minor deductions: no useCallback needed since there's no passed-down callback, but the pattern is reasonable; the escapeRegExp helper is defined but unused (dead code), which is a small code-quality ding; 'No results found' logic correctly gated on !isPending. Overall well-structured, syntactically valid, meets nearly all requirements cleanly.
